alternatives_considered: Launching full RFP to other RCM vendors
Migrating to athenaCollector only billing module
battlecards.why_selected: Provided retroactive rate reduction to 3.15 % of collections without triggering $9 M early-termination fee; lowest overall switching risk.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year addendum effective 9/1/2022 with 3.15 % fee tier, retroactive pricing credit, price lock through Jan 2025
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Benchmarks showed Advantia paying out-of-market rates; threat to issue RFP six months before 2025 renewal; early notice to avoid $9 M penalty highlighted win-win.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Fully integrated EHR/PM/RCM platform, embedded workflows already adopted by 75+ providers, avoids re-implementation.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Historically higher fees than market peers; aggressive termination penalties reduce flexibility.
battlecards.switching_costs: ~$9 M early termination charge plus major clinical/workflow change and data migration effort.
battlecards.notes: Savings scenario analysis (Slides 5) used $110 M collections baseline.

battlecards.why_selected: Most competitive BAFO pricing for Heartland region, agreed to formulary support and 60-day terms.
battlecards.contract_terms: Draft master distribution agreement— formulary & inventory management, dedicated implementation resources, QBRs; term 3 years (contract negotiations 8/22 & 9/16 updates).
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to award all Heartland volume; head-to-head pricing transparency from multi-round RFP.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Broad product portfolio, strong logistics, GPO pricing via Premier/Vizient.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Historically mixed service in Mid-Atlantic; higher minimums vs some competitors.
battlecards.switching_costs: System set-up, staff training on ordering portal, back-end contract price loads.
battlecards.notes: McKesson replaced Medline in Heartland while retaining Mid-Atlantic book, creating single enterprise partner per region.

battlecards.why_selected: Met minimum 10 % savings while avoiding operational disruption and LIS re-integration required for a switch.
battlecards.contract_terms: Pricing addendum locking BAFO rates; planned start 10/15/2022; term aligned to existing service agreements.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Quest’s 19 % cheaper proposal provided credible switch threat; incumbency not guaranteed.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Embedded phlebotomy staff, existing athenaNet interface, known service levels.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Initial pricing out of market; limited flexibility on certain high-volume tests.
battlecards.switching_costs: Re-credentialing, new courier routes, interface build/testing, practice staff retraining.
battlecards.notes: Savings reflected in Project Close-out slide 3; RFQ data slide 8 shows line-item comparisons.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Operational change deemed too disruptive despite higher savings; decision made to stay with incumbent LabCorp.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggressive BAFO pricing (19 % less than baseline) used to pressure incumbent.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Lowest evaluated pricing on key test SKUs; broad national footprint.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Required transition of phlebotomy services and new interfaces; uncertainty on service levels for Mid-Atlantic practices.
battlecards.switching_costs: Courier set-up, staff workflow changes, IT interface build.
battlecards.notes: Remained competitive option for future rebids.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Pay-per-scan model significantly more expensive than hybrid in-house solution; supplier unresponsive to scheduling & pricing discussions.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to bring sonography fully in-house and supplement with agency if needed.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Flexible per-scan billing, no upfront staffing costs.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: High per-scan rate ($50), limited responsiveness, no long-term cost control.
battlecards.switching_costs: Recruitment ramp-up and onboarding of full-time sonographers; need for supplemental agency coverage during transition.
battlecards.notes: Treya recommended Staffmark 20 % utilization to cover gaps during transition.
